sanskrit: saṃsam id yuvase vṛṣann agne viśvāny arya ā | iḍas pade sam idhyase sa no vasūny ā bhara ||
english: O mighty Agni, you yoke all things together for the lord; you are kindled in the seat of refreshment — bring us riches.

sanskrit: saṃ jānīdhvaṃ saṃ pṛcyadhvaṃ saṃ vo manāṃsi jānatām | devā bhāgaṃ yathā pūrve saṃjānānā upāsate ||
english: Be of one mind, be united, may your minds be in accord; as the gods of old, in concord, attend to their share.

sanskrit: samāno mantraḥ samitiḥ samānī samānaṃ cittaṃ saha vo manāṃsi | samānena vo haviṣā juhomi yathā saṃmanaso 'satha ||
english: Common is your prayer, common your assembly, common your mind — your thoughts together; with a common oblation I offer for you, that you may be of one accord.

sanskrit: ut sūryo diva eti puro viśvāni yo 'ruhat | ādityaḥ parvatāṅ ati viśvadṛṣṭo adṛṣṭahā ||
english: The sun rises across the sky, having mounted all the regions before; Āditya passes over the mountains, seen by all, the destroyer of the unseen evil.

sanskrit: āyurvidaṃ vipaścitaṃ śrutāṃ kaṇvasya vīrudham | āhārṣaṃ viśvabheṣajīm asyādṛṣṭān ni śamaya ||
english: I have brought the herb of Kaṇva, knowing the life-force, renowned, the all-healing plant — quell this person's unseen afflictions.

sanskrit: ni gāvo goṣṭhe asadan ni mṛgāso avikṣata | ni ketavo janānāṃ ny adṛṣṭā alipsata ||
english: The cows have settled in the cowpen, the wild beasts have rested; the banners of the people have been furled, the unseen evils have been checked.

sanskrit: himavataḥ pra sravatha tāḥ sindhum upa gacchatha | āpo gha mahyaṃ tad devīr dadan hṛddyotabheṣajam ||
english: You flow forth from the Himālaya and make your way to the Sindhu; those divine waters have surely given me that heart-illumining medicine.

sanskrit: yad akṣībhyām ādidyota pārṣṇibhyāṃ hṛdayena ca | āpas tat sarvaṃ niṣ karan tvaṣṭā riṣṭam ivānasaḥ ||
english: Whatever flashed through the eyes, through the heels, and through the heart — the waters have expelled all that, as Tvaṣṭṛ removes a defect from a cart.

sanskrit: sindhurājñīḥ sindhupatnīḥ sarvā yā nadya sthana | dattā nas tasya bheṣajaṃ tena vo bhunajāmahai ||
english: All you rivers, queens of the Sindhu, consorts of the Sindhu — give us the medicine for that; with it we shall enjoy your gift.

sanskrit: punantu mā devajanāḥ punantu manavo dhiyā | punantu viśvā bhūtāni pavamānaḥ punātu mā ||
english: May the divine hosts purify me, may the Manus purify me by thought, may all beings purify me — may the purifying stream purify me.

sanskrit: punātu mā pavamānaḥ kratve dakṣāya jīvase | jyok ca sūryāya dṛśe ||
english: May the purifying current purify me for will, for power, for life, and for long beholding of the sun.

sanskrit: ubhābhyāṃ deva savitaḥ pavitreṇa savena ca | asmān punīhi cakṣase ||
english: O divine Savitṛ, purify us with both — with the filter and with your impulse — for clear sight.

sanskrit: īrṣyāyā dhrājiṃ prathamām adhamām uttamām uta | manyuṃ hṛdayyaṃ śokaṃ taṃ te nir mantrayāmahe ||
english: The foremost dart of jealousy, the lowest and the highest — the wrath that dwells in the heart, the grief — these we charm out of you.

sanskrit: etad yat te hṛdi śritaṃ manaskaṃ patayiṣṇukam | tatas ta īrṣyāṃ muñcāmi nir ūṣmāṇaṃ dṛter iva ||
english: That which is lodged in your heart, tending toward the mind, about to fly — from that I release your jealousy, as steam is released from a skin.

sanskrit: yathā bhūmir mṛtamanā mṛtān mṛtamanastarā | yathota mamruṣo mana everṣyor mṛtaṃ manaḥ ||
english: As the earth is dead in mind toward the dead, more dead in mind than the dead — as the mind of a corpse is dead — so let the mind of jealousy be dead.

sanskrit: dyauś ca mā pṛthivī ca pracetasau śukro bṛhan dakṣiṇā mā pipartu | anu svadhā cikitāṃ somo agnir vāyur mā yātu savitā bhagaś ca ||
english: May Heaven and Earth, the two all-knowing ones, may the bright and great South wind carry me across; with awareness let Soma, Agni, Vāyu, Savitṛ, and Bhaga come along with the self-law.

sanskrit: punar manaḥ punar āyur na āgan punaś cakṣuḥ punar ākūtir āgan | vaiśvānaro no adabdhas tanūpā antas tiṣṭhāti duritād avadyāt ||
english: Mind has come back to us, life has come back, sight has come back, intention has come back; Vaiśvānara, undeceived, protector of the body, stands within, guarding from misfortune and from blame.

sanskrit: saṃ varcasā payasā saṃ tanūbhir aganmahi manasā saṃ śivena | tvaṣṭā sudatro varivaḥ kṛṇotv anūnas tāṣṭu tanvo viriṣṭam ||
english: We have come together with radiance, with vital sap, with our bodies, with the auspicious mind; may Tvaṣṭṛ, well-shaped, make wide room — let him fashion the body's injury into wholeness.

sanskrit: idaṃ tad yuja uttaraṃ yenendraṃ śumbhāmy aṣṭaye | asya kṣatraṃ śriyaṃ mahīṃ vṛṣṭir iva vardhayā tṛṇam ||
english: This is that superior yoke by which I adorn Indra for the conquest; increase his dominion, his glory, his greatness — as rain increases the grass.

sanskrit: asya kṣatram agnīṣomāv asya vardhayataṃ rayim | atho rāṣṭrasyābhīvarge kṛṇutaṃ yuja uttaram ||
english: O Agni and Soma, increase his sovereignty, increase his wealth; and for the supremacy of his kingdom make the yoke highest.

sanskrit: sabandhuś cāsabandhuś ca yo jāto yaś ca niṣṭiyaḥ | yajamānāya sunvate sarvaṃ taṃ rīradhāsi naḥ ||
english: Both the one with kin and the one without kin, the one born here and the one born outside — all of them you deliver to us, for the sacrificer who presses the soma.

sanskrit: yaśo bṛhad vardhatām indrajūtaṃ sahasrabhṛṣṭi sukṛtaṃ sahasvat | prasarsrāṇam anu dīrghāya jīvase haviṣmantaṃ vardhaya sarvatātaye ||
english: May great fame, driven by Indra, thousand-peaked, well-wrought, powerful, increase; flowing forth for long life — increase the oblation-bearer for all-round completeness.

sanskrit: yaśā indro yaśā agnir yaśāḥ somo ajāyata | yaśā viśvasya bhūtasya- -aham asmi yaśastamaḥ ||
english: Indra was born with glory, Agni with glory, Soma was born with glory; of all that exists I am the most glorious.

sanskrit: vayaṃ te agne yaśaso yaśobhir yaśasvino haviṣainā vidhema | sa no dhehi rāṣṭram indrajūtaṃ tava trātre adhivāke syāma ||
english: We, glorious, serve you, O Agni, the glorious one, with glories and with this oblation; grant us the kingdom driven by Indra — may we be under your protection, under your advocacy.

sanskrit: ava jyām iva dhanvano manyuṃ tanomi te hṛdaḥ | adhā saṃmanasau bhūtvā sakhikeva sacāvahai ||
english: I draw your wrath from your heart as one draws the bowstring from a bow; then, becoming of one mind, we two shall go together like friends.

sanskrit: vi te manyuṃ nayāmasi sakhikeva sacāvahai | adhas te aśmanā manyuṃ guruṇābhi ni dadhmasi ||
english: We lead your anger away so we two may go together like friends; with a heavy stone we press your wrath down below.

sanskrit: abhi tiṣṭhāmi te manyuṃ pārṣṇibhyāṃ prapadābhyām | parā te daṇḍyaṃ vadhaṃ parā manyuṃ suvāmi te ||
english: I tread upon your anger with both heels and forefeet; I drive away from you the rod-worthy blow, I drive away your wrath.

sanskrit: hiraṇyayaḥ panthā āsīd aritrāṇi hiraṇyayā | nāvo hiraṇyayīr āsan yābhiḥ kuṣṭhaṃ nirāvaham ||
english: The path was golden, the oars were golden, the boats were golden by which I brought kuṣṭha here.

sanskrit: suparṇasuvane girau jātaṃ himavatas pari | dhanair abhi śrutaṃ yanti kuṣṭhehi takmanāśanaḥ ||
english: Born on the mountain where the suparṇa bird cries, born around the Himālaya — they come famed with riches: O kuṣṭha, come here, destroyer of fever.

sanskrit: yo giriṣu jāyase vīrudhāṃ balavattamaḥ | kuṣṭhehi takmanāśana takmānaṃ nāśayann itaḥ ||
english: You who are born in the mountains, mightiest of herbs — O kuṣṭha, come here, destroyer of fever, driving fever away from here.

sanskrit: idāvatsarāya parivatsarāya saṃvatsarāya kṛṇutā bṛhan namaḥ | teṣāṃ vayaṃ sumatau yajñiyānām api bhadre saumanase syāma ||
english: Make great obeisance to the Idāvatsara, the Parivatsara, and the Saṃvatsara; may we be in the good favor of those worthy of sacrifice, in their auspicious goodwill.

sanskrit: ye vaḥ panthā bahavo devayānā anu dyāvāpṛthivī saṃcarantī | teṣām ajyāniṃ yatamo na āvahāt tasmai no devāḥ pari dhatta sarve ||
english: Your many god-trodden paths that pass along Heaven and Earth — whichever of these may bring us victory, may all the gods surround us for that one.

sanskrit: śarad dhemantaḥ śiśiro vasanto grīṣmo varṣāḥ suvite no dadhāta | ā no goṣu bhajatauṣadhīṣu nivāta id vaḥ śaraṇe syāma ||
english: Autumn, winter, the cool season, spring, summer, the rains — set us in good course; grant us a share in cattle and in plants — only in a sheltered place may we dwell in your shelter.

sanskrit: vaiśvānaro na ūtaya ā pra yātu parāvataḥ | agnir ukthair no aṃhasaḥ ||
english: Let Vaiśvānara come forth to us with help from afar; may Agni with hymns free us from distress.

sanskrit: vaiśvānaro na ā gamad imaṃ yajñaṃ sajūr upa- | -imāṃ suṣṭutiṃ mama ||
english: May Vaiśvānara come to us, together attending this sacrifice and my praise-song.

sanskrit: vaiśvānaro no aṅgirobhi stomaṃ yajñaṃ ca cākl̥pat | aiṣu dyumnaṃ svar yamat ||
english: May Vaiśvānara along with the Aṅgirasas fashion our praise-song and sacrifice; may he seize brilliant light and the sun among these.

sanskrit: ajaiṣaṃ tvā saṃlikhitam ajaiṣam uta saṃrudham | aviṃ vṛko yathā mathad evā mathnāmi te kṛtam ||
english: I have conquered you when scratched, I have conquered you when blocked; as a wolf churns a sheep, so I churn what you have done.

sanskrit: yathā vṛkṣam aśanir viśvahā hanty aprati | evāham amuṃ kitavam akṣair vadhyāsam aprati ||
english: As a thunderbolt always strikes a tree without resistance, so may I strike that gambler with the dice, without resistance.

sanskrit: turāṇām aturāṇāṃ viśāṃ devayatīnām | sam aitu viśvato bhago antarhastaṃ kṛtaṃ mama ||
english: From the swift and the slow, from the clans that seek the gods — may fortune come together from all sides; what is made is in my hand.

sanskrit: yāvad dyaur yāvat pṛthivī yāvad ābhāti sūryaḥ | tāvat sṛjāmi te viṣaṃ yāvad arṣanti sindhavaḥ ||
english: As long as the sky endures, as long as the earth, as long as the sun shines — for that long I release poison into you, as long as the rivers flow.

sanskrit: ucchvasanta ud īrate gāva āvasathād iva | ahīnāṃ paśyatā viṣam apavaktā na vidyate ||
english: They rise up breathing out like cattle from the stall; of the snakes that are seen, the poison has no one to speak it away.

sanskrit: ā jaghāna pṛṣaddhanuḥ saṅgathe dhamanīnām | mūrdhānaṃ viṣam āskadya- -aṅgāni vy asisrasat ||
english: The speckle-bowed one struck at the junction of the arteries; the poison leapt to the head and scattered through the limbs.

sanskrit: mā no devā ahir vadhīt santokān sahapūruṣān | saṃyataṃ na vi ṣparad vyāttaṃ na saṃ yamat ||
english: May the serpent not slay us, O gods, us with our offspring, together with our men; let it not spread what is closed, let it not close what is open.

sanskrit: saṃ te dadhāmi dadbhir dataḥ saṃ te hanvā hanū | saṃ te jihvayā jihvāṃ saṃ ta āsnāha āsyam ||
english: I set tooth against your teeth, I set jaw against your jaws; I set tongue against your tongue, I set mouth against your mouth.

sanskrit: namo 'haye asitāya namas tiraścirājaye | svajāya babhrave namo namo devajanebhyaḥ ||
english: Homage to the dark serpent, homage to the king who goes sideways; homage to the coiling tawny one, homage to the divine folk.
